critical_code_review_comments: Login regression risk: iter292 successfully logged cathy@example.com in for its 3 completed tools (CE / PC / BC). This iteration's failure suggests something changed on the auth path between iter292 and iter293. Given the review-request's context note ('reverted all tool-output panels from solid .panel-solid-* back to light .sect-* / .bg-surface cards') this shouldn't have touched auth — check if any other unintended change landed (e.g. axios base URL, auth interceptor, cookie/localStorage change) or if backend /api/auth/login is 5xx.

The paywall lock card shown on 4 gated tools has GOOD legibility (light bg-surface card, dark serif heading, muted body, teal underlined 'Sign in' link, clay 'Start free 7-day trial' CTA) — no legibility issue there; this is just noted so it isn't misread as an intentional design change to the tool output panels.

Statement Decoder loader UX: the 92-second countdown while 'Decoding your statement...' is visible is prominent but not obviously reassuring — copy might benefit from a 'typical time ~60s' hint or a spinner-with-percent, since a 90s wait with only a running counter feels like it could hang.
